headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors from shared filesystem and broad egress; Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side code amplifies Plandex’s write-capable workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can read/write the server filesystem and chain tools in graph flows, while Plandex reads/writes a project directory and accepts stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible content bridge where attacker-controlled files or outputs from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is not fully documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF Langflow flow nodes ingest files produced by Plandex without sanitization, injection is reachable.
IF Plandex consumes Langflow-generated text as plan input, instruction hijacking is possible.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of cross-agent text artifacts.
Add a strict delimiter/schema for inter-agent handoff files.
Review any prompt-bearing files before passing them between agents.
Use separate directories with read-only handoff copies.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem access, and Langflow explicitly touches flow inputs/intermediate outputs while Plandex touches source code. If they share a workspace or server-side store, sensitive code or flow data can flow into either agent’s outbound API calls. The shared-state details are documented only at profile level, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or shared backend state, leakage becomes plausible.
IF either agent forwards file contents to external model providers, sensitive material can leave the environment.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces and credentials.
Turn off auto-upload of file contents where possible.
Restrict outbound domains to approved model providers only.
Redact secrets from shared artifacts before handoff.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands and write the filesystem; Plandex can also modify git state. In a shared directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state, and Langflow’s server-side code component is unsandboxed by default. This matches the high-risk overlap pattern because defaults are dangerous and the blast radius can be irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, write conflicts are likely.
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while Langflow runs unsandboxed code, state corruption can occur.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate writable directory.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex during concurrent runs.
Run Langflow code components in a sandbox or container.
Serialize filesystem mutations with an external lock.
requires-engineering: add transactional git/worktree coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and tools, and Plandex uses review-then-apply with optional auto-apply. If Langflow-produced outputs are fed into Plandex plans without verification, errors can cascade into code changes or other actions. Plandex’s review step reduces risk somewhat, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Langflow outputs are used as authoritative inputs to Plandex plans, errors can propagate.
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled, unverified upstream mistakes can become committed changes.
mitigations: Require human review of Langflow outputs before Plandex ingestion.
Disable Plandex auto-apply for shared workflows.
Add a verification step that checks claims against source artifacts.
Use structured outputs instead of free-form text handoff.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only document generic flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and source code; no explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch is stated. The main compliance concern is policy drift in shared logs or retention, but the profiles do not show a concrete default breach. Because evidence is limited, keep this low rather than none.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared logs or retained outputs, policy mismatch may arise.
IF deployment regions differ between the two backends, residency controls may be violated.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared artifacts.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document the data classes each agent may touch.
Review backend regions before deployment.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and retention controls.
